## Mackensen's 3 November withdrawal report and its separately received ninth part

<a id="mackensens-november-3-withdrawal-report-and-its-separately-received-ninth-part"></a>

**Sources on this page:** p113 A3, p113 B9.

**Related source pages:** [p114 A1](114.md#source-p114-a1), [p114 A4](114.md#source-p114-a4), [p115 A5](115.md#source-p115-a5), [p115 A6](115.md#source-p115-a6), [p115 A7](115.md#source-p115-a7), [p115 A8](115.md#source-p115-a8), [p116 A10](116.md#source-p116-a10), [p116 A11](116.md#source-p116-a11), [p116 A12](116.md#source-p116-a12), [p116 A13](116.md#source-p116-a13).

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-withdrawal-report-mackensens-november-3-withdrawal-report-and-its-separately-received-ninth-part"></a>



**Source edition and assembly audit: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This thirteen-part report assesses threats to the occupation army's rear
communications and proposes immediate withdrawal from Romania if a general
armistice is not expected soon. Its historical decipherment belongs to
**J. Rives Childs**; **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**
published most of the reconstructed body in their 2016 paper, Table 3.
The present contribution is an exact source edition, repair accounting,
and the recovery of the report's assembly from separately received pieces.

The original package below retains **twelve physical parts**: eleven readable
editions and one heavily jammed ending. The separately received
[second part, p118 A2](118.md#edition-cases-military-mackensen-withdrawal-part2), has now been located
and source-reviewed, so all thirteen numbered parts have a source entry.
Its 189-position reading uses one explicitly modeled missing coordinate
and thirteen observed-coordinate substitutions; its place-name defects
remain literal. The original twelve-record evidence and totals below stay
unchanged, and the second part has its own repair certificate.
The period square and column ranks remain the published **Nov1–3** key.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-withdrawal-report-why-part-9-belongs-here"></a>

### Identification of the ninth part

The consecutive copy on printed pp114–116 explicitly marks its ninth part
missing. Table 3 in the 2016 paper also leaves it missing. But the previous
source page contains **p113 B, explicitly labelled `9 TL`**. It shares the
`2000 (3)` message reference, the OHL destination, the Nov1–3 cipher key,
and the exact grammatical join from part 8 to part 10. Its receiving time is
9.38pm on 5 November, after the 4 November main copy; the later receipt
explains why it is treated as a separate physical witness rather than
silently inserted into the page image.

Part 8 ends with the communications that had so far been disabled only
because of something; part 9 supplies the complete collapse of the Hungarian
army and disorganization of its railway system; part 10 continues with a
threat of enemy attack. The new ninth-part edition needs **zero changes
to its 216 observed coordinates** and yields 108 fixed plaintext labels.
This is a source-and-assembly result, not a claim of universal decipherment
priority over earlier historical work or the earlier unreviewed OCR candidate.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-withdrawal-report-read-the-surviving-parts"></a>

### Read the surviving parts

Spaces below are editorial word breaks. Literal `X` separators, abbreviations,
repetitions, unresolved `?` positions and the named defects are preserved.
Removing spaces from each displayed reading reproduces its certified
plaintext exactly. Ordinary word repairs are priced in the table below;
the complete unchanged raw strings remain in the certificate.

**Raw output:**

The source prints 160 slots against RICHI-222 and explicitly says “Balance jammed.” The stated tail-loss model appends 62 unknown coordinates. Only 38 of 111 plaintext positions are fixed, and **no source mask, lost coordinate or word is filled**. The existing historical translation is not converted into invented cipher evidence.

A [separately priced optional route fragment](../experiments/p116_optional_route_fragment/README.md)
tests five word spans under this same tail-loss model. It fixes 75 of 111
positions through five printed-mask fills and 32 lost-tail fills, without
changing any observed coordinate. Each of the 37 selected letters retains
one observed half-pair. The historical English translation guided the word
choices; it is not an independent German coordinate witness. The army label,
approval clause and footer are unfilled in that layer, and the raw-only edition
above is unchanged.

**Approval-request extension.** A further [conditional word layer](../experiments/p116_optional_route_fragment/approval-request.md)
adds `EINVERSTAENDNIS?ERBETEN`, raising the reading to **90/111 positions**
with zero observed-coordinate changes, 11 printed-mask fills and 43 lost-tail
fills in total. Of the 15 newly fixed letters, 13 have an observed half-pair;
V at 68 and N at 87 are wholly missing and supplied by the word proposal.
Position 80 stays unresolved. An optional additional S gives 91/111 for one
more lost-tail fill; the army label and footer remain open.

**Optional footer fields.** The [joined field proposal](../experiments/p116_optional_route_fragment/footer.md)
adds `XKXMXRMX1XA` from overlapping original fields in p164 D and p105 C1,
reaching **97/111 positions** with 12 printed-mask fills and 49 lost-tail fills.
A separate closing proposal, guided by the historical signature, adds
`GR?XOPX` and reaches **101/111**, with 12 printed-mask fills and 53 lost-tail
fills. All eleven new labels have an observed half-coordinate; no observation
changes. The preceding position, intervening labels and army designation remain
unfilled. These are contextual proposals, not repeated-message identifications.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-withdrawal-report-the-two-short-frames-require-different-qualifications"></a>

### The two short frames require different qualifications

Part 11 actually prints 219 slots, although its header says 220. An independent
manual retranscription confirms the four-character group `VGGV` at source
index 110. Testing **all 220 one-coordinate insertion boundaries** against
the readable template yields a unique zero-observed-substitution fit at
boundary 102. Masking the whole `WAFFENSTILLSTAND` word leaves the same minimum.
The five boundaries in or after the visibly short group,110–114, need 8,8,9,9
and 10 observed-coordinate changes under the complete template.

Thus the chosen model is arithmetically economical, but its missing-coordinate
location is **not visually witnessed by the short group**. A separate source
review found no transcription correction that removes this tension. The
edition does not infer how the historical printer or operator produced it.

Part 12 actually prints 237 against 238. Its short group `DDGF` starts at 140.
All 238 single-loss boundaries were evaluated. Boundaries141,142,143 and 144
tie at three observed-coordinate changes; these positions fall within or
at the end of that short group. After masking `BESATZUNSHEER`, three of those
boundaries remain tied at two observed changes. None is promoted to a
uniquely witnessed missing-symbol location.

Both templates were formed after reading the source and the prior report.
These are exact conditional cost comparisons, not blind confirmation of
the missing-coordinate mechanism or historical wording. The certificate
retains all 458 gap comparisons, all tied raw readings, and the separate
short-group comparisons.

The source-derived part 12 wording is `ZEIT ZU ERWARTEN IST`, where Table 3
uses `ZEIT EINTRITT`. This edition follows the received coordinate evidence.
Similarly, source defects and the uncertain part 10 reference are retained
instead of importing every normalization from the later reconstruction.

## p113 C — Poti tobacco loading inquiry, with literal quantity 2400

**Edition context:** Tobacco ready for loading at Poti: a 3 November inquiry.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-nov3-poti-tobacco-loading-tobacco-ready-for-loading-at-poti-a-november-3-inquiry"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p113 section C reports tobacco at Poti ready for loading and asks
when loading will be possible. Its native **212-slot frame** gives **106/106
fixed output positions** under the unchanged published **Nov1–3** key. The
edited reading makes **one observed-coordinate substitution**, supported by
an unedited repetition of the same abbreviation at the end of the message.
There are no source-mask fills, insertions, deletions or source reorderings.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p113_reviewed.png](../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/sources/p113_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).
<a id="source-p113-c"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-naval-nov3-poti-tobacco-loading-p113-c"></a>

### p113 C

[Reviewed source image — source-PDF reference](../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — header:**

```text
Page heading: 3rd NOVEMBER, 1918.
C) POT v NKJ (8.42 a.m., November 4th)
SS FÜR POT V OSM (3) 1430
RICHI-212
```

</details>

The embedded `28X10` is retained as a separate date-like label. Its readable
rendering as `28/10` does not replace the 3 November page heading or
4 November intercept date. The literal header and complete grouped
ciphertext are preserved in the
[inputs](../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/inputs.json).

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 212-slot frame; 106/106 fixed positions:**

```text
28X10XSCHUTZOFFZRSCHIFFZAUSGLXPOTIXKXAXSAGTPOTI2400TONSTABAKVERLADEBEREITXWANVERLADGMOEGLICHXSCHIFFSAUSGLX
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution; no fills; 106/106 fixed positions:**

```text
28X10XSCHUTZOFFZRSCHIFFSAUSGLXPOTIXKXAXSAGTPOTI2400TONSTABAKVERLADEBEREITXWANVERLADGMOEGLICHXSCHIFFSAUSGLX
```

</details>

The proposed change is **source index 81 F→V**, changing the first
`SCHIFFZAUSGL` to `SCHIFFSAUSGL`. The closing raw `SCHIFFSAUSGL` already
supplies this spelling without any repair. The exact internal match and
complete re-encryption are checked in the certificate; this is a local
editorial proposal, not a change to the key or the literal transcription.

**Readable German — complete edited stream, with spacing and punctuation only:**

> 28/10. Schutzoffz. R. Schiffsausgl. Poti. K. A. sagt Poti 2400 Tons Tabak verladebereit. Wan Verladg moeglich. Schiffsausgl.

The isolated **R**, the abbreviation **K. A.**, the single-N spelling **Wan**
and the shortened **Verladg** remain visible. The text does not silently
supply a second N, turn R into a separator, or expand an abbreviation into
an identified office. `2400` is the literal numerical field returned by
the published square; its historical numeral assignment is not independently
proved by this reading.

**Meaning:** A report that tobacco is ready to load at Poti is followed by
an inquiry about when loading will be possible. The message reports
readiness and asks a question; it does not establish that a shipment left,
identify a vessel, or authenticate the quantity independently of the
cipher's numerical labels.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-nov3-poti-tobacco-loading-source-restoration-and-prior-credit"></a>

### Source restoration and prior credit

The source's final row visibly prints **ADVXD**. Earlier repository OCR had
**ADV?D**. Restoring that observed X gives the complete native raw reading;
it is an OCR correction, not a supplied historical coordinate. The old OCR
block is frozen with its recomputed unchanged-key output in
[prior candidates](../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/prior_candidates.json).

J. Rives Childs's historical scan remains the source. Published period-key
recovery by George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, and Lasry's
2017 key list, retain their credit. This is a source-reviewed edition and
explicitly priced word repair; no first-decipherment priority is asserted.

[Inputs](../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/inputs.json),
[certificates](../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/certificates.json)
and [reproduction instructions](../experiments/nov3_poti_tobacco_loading/README.md)
preserve the key, all source and plaintext positions, the one changed
coordinate, the internal word witness and a complete re-encryption.

## p113 D1 — Eilvese/OUI transmission modes and provisional traffic times, with literal labels

**Edition context:** Eilvese/OUI: transmission arrangements and provisional traffic times.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov3-eilvese-traffic-schedule-eilveseoui-transmission-arrangements-and-provisional-traffic-times"></a>



**Source edition and verification: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p113 section D, part 1, gives transmission and reception arrangements
for **Eilvese/OUI**, followed by provisional transmitting windows. A repeated
source group and its adjacent damaged group create a length conflict:
**362 printed slots** appear under **RIZI-352**. An explicitly conditional
exclusion of ten slots produces a complete **176-position raw reading**
under the unchanged published **Nov1–3** key.

Two ordinary-word repairs, **UNGEDAENPFT→UNGEDAEMPFT** and **BIX→BIS**, cost
**3 observed-coordinate substitutions**. The primary frame needs **no
coordinate fills**. It excludes **7 observed coordinates and 3 printed
dashes**, counted separately from those three word-repair substitutions.
All equally priced frame alternatives are retained. Numerical labels,
including the unusual **3X13**, remain literal.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p113_D1_reviewed.png](../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/sources/p113_D1_reviewed.png) · [p113_D1_repetition_detail.png](../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/sources/p113_D1_repetition_detail.png). [File and pixel verification](../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).

**Raw output — conditional ten-slot exclusion; 176/176 fixed positions:**

```text
EILVESEXOUIXSENDETABX3X13X12XNACHTSXUNGEDAENPFTANSIEMITWELLE9500XOUIEMPFAENGTSIEWELLEX4250XTOENENDXXVORLAUFIGEVERKEHRSZEITENXXOUIXSENDET12NACHTSBIX0100X0330BIS0345X0530BIS0600X
```

**Edited output — the same conditional frame; 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and no fills; 176/176 fixed positions:**

```text
EILVESEXOUIXSENDETABX3X13X12XNACHTSXUNGEDAEMPFTANSIEMITWELLE9500XOUIEMPFAENGTSIEWELLEX4250XTOENENDXXVORLAUFIGEVERKEHRSZEITENXXOUIXSENDET12NACHTSBIS0100X0330BIS0345X0530BIS0600X
```

</details>

**Readable German — complete conditional edited stream, with literal labels and spelling retained:**

> Eilvese. OUI sendet ab 3X13, 12 nachts, ungedaempft an Sie mit Welle 9500. OUI empfaengt Sie Welle 4250, toenend. Vorlaufige Verkehrszeiten: OUI sendet 12 nachts bis 0100, 0330 bis 0345, 0530 bis 0600.

**Meaning:** The telegram sets out sending and receiving arrangements for
Eilvese/OUI and provisional transmitting windows. It uses the technical
terms *ungedaempft* and *toenend*. The stated numerical fields and windows
are reported as transmitted labels; the edition does not independently
authenticate their numerical assignments, add a wavelength unit or a time
zone, or establish that the schedule was implemented.

The field **3X13** is not converted into a plausible date. **Vorlaufige**
keeps the source's encoded spelling without silently adding E or changing
it into an umlauted form. All values **9500**, **4250**, **12**, **0100**,
**0330**, **0345**, **0530** and **0600** remain unchanged.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov3-eilvese-traffic-schedule-coordinate-costs-and-complete-frame-alternatives"></a>

### Coordinate costs and complete frame alternatives

The word repairs affect two plaintext positions but three observed
coordinates:

| Original source index | Model index after exclusion | Observed-coordinate change |
| ---: | ---: | --- |
| 4 | 4 | G→D |
| 321 | 311 | X→V |
| 348 | 338 | G→V |

The certificate maps each changed pair to its raw and proposed plaintext
letter. It fully re-encrypts the complete 176-position candidate. This
checks the explicit proposal and its source price; it does not turn the
exclusion hypothesis into a visible historical correction.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov3-eilvese-traffic-schedule-every-consecutive-ten-slot-exclusion"></a>

#### Every consecutive ten-slot exclusion

All **353** possible consecutive ten-slot exclusions are compared against
the fixed complete candidate. The minimum is **3 observed-coordinate
substitutions**, attained by starts **172–185 inclusive**. These frames
have different additional source-mask-fill and exclusion costs:

| Exclusion start | Retained source masks that must be filled | Observed coordinates excluded |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 172 or 185 | 3 | 10 |
| 173 or 184 | 2 | 9 |
| 174 or 183 | 1 | 8 |
| Any start from 175 through 182 | 0 | 7 |

All rows exclude ten source slots and require the same minimum observed
substitution count. The **eight no-fill starts 175–182** produce exactly
the same retained ciphertext and raw plaintext. Their source-to-model
mappings differ, so every alias remains in the certificate. The displayed
start 175 is the natural whole-group choice, not a uniquely determined
historical location.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov3-eilvese-traffic-schedule-every-pair-of-complete-five-slot-groups"></a>

#### Every pair of complete five-slot groups

The verifier also compares all **2,556** ways to exclude two of the 72
complete five-slot groups, retaining the final two-character `AV` group.
Three pairs attain the same three-substitution minimum:

| Group starts in original source | Source-mask fills | Observed coordinates excluded |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 175 and 180 | 0 | 7 |
| 180 and 185 | 0 | 7 |
| 185 and 190 | 3 | 10 |

The first two remove `DG---` and one of the two copies of `FAGVD`; they
produce the same complete raw stream. The third remains a recorded minimum
of the observed-substitution objective, but retains all three dashes and
requires their values to be supplied. It is not silently discarded from
the comparison.

These are **fixed-candidate comparisons** within two stated families.
Arbitrary ten-position subsets and all other possible plaintexts have not
been exhausted. The repeated group, advertised length and strong body
reading support this reconstruction, while the absence of an explicit
cancellation keeps the frame conditional.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov3-eilvese-traffic-schedule-source-restoration-attribution-and-reproduction"></a>

### Source restoration, attribution and reproduction

Earlier repository OCR supplied **355 slots**, omitting the visible
`DG---` group and final `AV` and masking several printed coordinates.
The reviewed 362-slot transcription restores those marks first; the later
ten-slot exclusion is a separate operation. The frozen old input and its
recomputed unchanged-key output remain available in
[prior candidates](../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/prior_candidates.json).

J. Rives Childs's scan is the historical source. Published period-key
recovery by George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker, Lasry's
2017 key list, and earlier repository work retain their credit. The current
work supplies a source edition, bounded frame comparisons and explicitly
priced word repairs. It asserts **no first-decipherment priority**.

[Inputs](../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/inputs.json),
[certificates](../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/certificates.json),
and [reproduction instructions](../experiments/nov3_eilvese_traffic_schedule/README.md)
preserve the native reading, exact crops, every retained and excluded source
position, all minimum-frame aliases and full candidate re-encryption.
